https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Cir.a:does: A CIRCLE NAME A HOLDER MAY LABEL A PARTY WITH, FOR THE HOLDER'S OWN KNOWING: each instance is ONE label (Personal · 1st Connection, Personal · Inner Circle, Professional · 1st Connection, Professional · Inner Circle). 🔴 A LABEL ONLY: it grants no access, reaches nobody and changes no rung. Writing it adds nobody to any audience set and writes no a:audienceRungMember, no a:directReader for the party, no a:readerGroup, no a:vaultReader and no a:visibilityTier on anything the holder keeps; authorization reads only those grant predicates, so it reads nothing from this. It shares its WORDS with the four Grantee terms (t/PersonalCloseCircleGrantee and its three siblings) but is ⛔ NOT one of them and carries ⛔ NONE of a:audienceContext, a:audienceDepth or a:audienceRungUnionOf, which are what make the platform read a term as a rung. Marking a contact 'Professional · Inner Circle' does not make them one of the holder's Professional Inner Circle audience; that is a PLACEMENT in MyNet (a membership of a principal in the holder's set), a different act with a different effect. ⛔ NOT a relationship kind (t/RelationshipKind: Customer, Friend). ⛔ A label is an INSTANCE of this type, never a sub-type.
a:example: Personal · 1st Connection: a friend the holder knows personally
Professional · Inner Circle: a colleague the holder works with closely
⛔ not the grant 'the people in my Professional Inner Circle may read this field': that is t/ProfessionalCloseCircleGrantee, with reach

https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Cir.a:label: Circle Label
https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Cir.a:placementNote: ROLE: ENTITY Type (a catalogue of labels), parent t/Information; Function Inform INHERITED; Value t/ContactLabelAccessNeutralityRate attached. Four entries. The four rung terms are NOT reused as the range of a label attribute: one term would then mean a grant in a:visibilityTier and a label in a:circleLabel (RuleBpontHomonym), and a reader that treats every reference to a Grantee term as a grant would over-reach.
https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Cir.a:premodNote: Adversarial pre-moderation, 2026-10-16, GET only. (1) DUPLICATE? /base/a/ 404 for circleLabel, contactKind, relationshipKind, connectionKind, circle; /base/t/ 404 for CircleLabel. (2) REUSE OF THE FOUR GRANTEE TERMS REFUSED, ON MEANING AND ON RISK. (3) SEPARATE FROM t/RelationshipKind ON PURPOSE: a shared catalogue with an axis marker would put 'Customer' beside 'Professional · Inner Circle' in one list and make every reader filter on the marker; a forgotten filter would offer a circle word where a relationship word belongs, and the circle words are the ones that look like access.

https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Rel.a:does: A KIND OF RELATIONSHIP A HOLDER MAY SAY A PARTY HAS TO THEM, FOR THE HOLDER'S OWN KNOWING: each instance is ONE kind (Customer, Prospect, Supplier, Partner, Friend, Family, Colleague, Advisor, Competitor, Investor, Public authority, Non-profit). It says what the party is TO THE HOLDER ('a customer of mine'), and which kinds make sense for which sort of party is carried by a:playableBy on the entry. 🔴 A LABEL ONLY: it grants no access, reaches nobody and changes no rung. Writing it adds nobody to any audience set and writes no a:audienceRungMember, no a:directReader for the party, no a:readerGroup, no a:vaultReader and no a:visibilityTier on anything the holder keeps; authorization reads only those grant predicates, so it reads nothing from this. ⛔ NEVER A RECORD TYPE: a kind does not change what the record IS (a Person stays a t:Person whether labelled Friend or Supplier); a record's NATURE is its type (t:AiAgent, t:DataStore), and the master already has those, so an AI agent is chosen as a type and is never a kind. ⛔ NOT t/Customer (a Planguage example stakeholder role in a specification, a Stakeholder sub-type); a kind named Customer is this catalogue's entry and is found by its type. ⛔ NOT t/Stakeholder or a role in a Value's Stakeholder line ('Kai as Owner', t/PartyMemberOf). ⛔ NOT a circle label (t/CircleLabel). ⛔ A kind is an INSTANCE, never a sub-type. HOLDER-DEFINED KINDS: a holder may add their own entries of this type in their OWN vault (no mint); they are the holder's alone and appear beside these on the holder's cards.
a:example: Customer: a party that buys from the holder (applies to a person or an organization)
Friend: a person the holder counts as a friend (applies to a person)
Competitor: an organization the holder competes with (applies to an organization)
⛔ not 'AI agent': that is a record type, t:AiAgent

https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Rel.a:label: Relationship Kind
https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Rel.a:placementNote: ROLE: ENTITY Type (a catalogue of kinds), parent t/Information; Function Inform INHERITED; Value t/ContactLabelAccessNeutralityRate attached. Twelve entries. APPLICABILITY REUSES a:playableBy (a relation asserted on a role-like term R pointing at a type T: an instance of T, or of a type under T, may play R): the entry 'Friend' is playable-by t/Person, 'Customer' by t/Person and t/Organization. No new applicability term. Only Person and Organization kinds are minted now; systems carry no relationship kind (their sub-kinds are record types).
https://ontology.example.test/base/t/Rel.a:premodNote: Adversarial pre-moderation, 2026-10-16, GET only. (1) DUPLICATE? /base/a/ 404 for relationshipKind; /base/t/ 404 for RelationshipKind; /base/terms?q= for customer, prospect, friend, family, colleague, partner, supplier, advisor, competitor, investor, non-profit finds no kind or relationship term. (2) HOMONYM: the label 'Customer' equals t/Customer (Suggested, a Stakeholder sub-type, 'a customer/shopper role ... cares about the count of items in their container (cart)'): different meaning, different kind of term (an entry versus a type), recorded here and in the entry; 'Authority' is avoided for t/Authority (Approved) and the entry is labelled 'Public authority'. (3) SEPARATE FROM t/CircleLabel (see there).
